Granny Willa sits in the front row in her patchwork shawl. Saffron lies along the back wall, and the clever rabbit sits on her tail. I sit with everyone, and Nib stands on the stage in his red cape. Haru tells part of The Boy and the Stone Giant. Riko tells part of The Lighthouse Cat. Birimo tells The Dragon Who Sneezed Glitter, and everyone laughs. Kiko tells the end of her story, and the hall goes quiet. Then Nib says, Every one of us has a story to tell. Say it with me. Every one of us has a story to tell. Wonderful! Let's read the festival program. "The Storytelling Festival of the Labyrinth of Tales. Welcome to the Central Hall! Today, four young storytellers will share the stories they wrote here. Haru: The Boy and the Stone Giant, a tale about a lonely giant who learns to laugh. Riko: The Lighthouse Cat, a tale about a small cat with a big heart. Birimo: The Dragon Who Sneezed Glitter, a very funny tale. Please don't sit too close! Kiko: The Girl Who Talked to the Wind, a tale about friendship and listening. Please listen quietly, and cheer at the end of each story. When the last story is told, keep your eyes on the Storybook." Who tells the funny tale? Birimo. What should the audience do at the end of each story? Cheer. The cheers are loud and happy. Then the sixth golden page appears: The sixth secret of stories: every one of us has a story to tell. The Storybook is complete! It glows like a little sun. As Nib closes it, a pressed purple flower falls out with a note. It says, Come to the Highlands of the Heart. We remember the green hills from the window. Our next adventure is waiting! Now, phonics. Let's review. Lanterns glimmer in the dark. Old doors creak. The voice in the dark whispered one word, pause, welcome. Kiko told her story bravely. The idea came to her like a shooting star. Goodbye, Nib! Thank you, Granny Willa! Thank you, Labyrinth of Tales!
